rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Throne and prophets exemplify elevated ranks among realms and rational beings, indirectly ridiculing polytheists who rejected a human prophet as unworthy.
rows.anchor: وقد ضرب لهم العرش والأنبياء مثلين لرفع الدرجات في العوالم والعقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After portraying prophetic rank, the discourse turns from prophethood to warning about Judgment, resuming the interrupted account of the Day of Recompense after 40:12.
rows.anchor: وتخلص من ذكر النبوءة إلى النذارة بيوم الجزاء ليعود وصف يوم الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inzār reports what is frightening, the opposite of glad tidings, which report what brings joy.
rows.anchor: والإنذار : إخبار فيه تحذير مما يسوء ، وهو ضد التبشير إذ هو إخبار بما فيه مسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza makes form IV transitive; normally it takes as object the person who was the subject of the basic verb.
rows.anchor: والهمزة في أنذر للتعدية فحقه أن لا يتعدى بالهمزة إلا إلى مفعول واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic usage incorporates the sense of warning, so the verb takes a second object rather than marking the reported danger with bi-.
rows.anchor: غير أنه غلب في الاستعمال تضمينه معنى التحذير فعدوه إلى مفعول ثان وهو استعمال القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the opening of al-Aʿrāf, bi- in the phrase about warning means cause or metaphorical instrument, not an object marker; its pronoun refers to the Book.
rows.anchor: فالباء فيه للسببية أو الآلة المجازية وليست للتعدية . وضمير به عائدا إلى الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden subject of warn could refer to Allah in 40:14, but Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers the relative pronoun in 40:15: the Prophet is the current warner, which also explains the explicit divine name in 40:16.
rows.anchor: والأحسن أن يعود على { من } الموصولة لينذر من ألقى عليه الروح قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-talāqī is the gathering day because all people meet there.
rows.anchor: وسمي يوم التلاقي لأن الناس كلهم يلتقون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the day people meet their Lord metaphorically by standing directly in His presence; Ibn ʿĀshūr links this usage to Jonah 10:7.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم يلقون ربهم لقاء مجازيا ، أي يقفون في حضرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm al-talāqī is the second object of warn; the first object, people, is omitted as obvious.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { يوم التلاقي } على أنه مفعول ثان ل { ينذر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words talāqī and yulqī form paronomasia.
rows.anchor: وبين { التلاقي } و { يلقي } جناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muṣḥaf writes al-talāqī without yāʾ; Nāfiʿ and a transmission from Abū ʿAmr read it with kasra and no yāʾ, while the other readers retain yāʾ in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وكتب { التلاقي } في المصحف بدون ياء . وقرأه نافع وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the word occurs in connected speech, dropping its yāʾ lacks a reason except treating connection as pause, rare in prose; the transmissions of Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr suffice as attestation.
rows.anchor: لأنه وقع في الوصل لا في الوقف فلا موجب لطرح الياء إلا معاملة الوصل معاملة الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm hum bārizūn is an apposition to Yawm al-talāqī; it is a nominal clause in a future time adverb without ellipsis, the stronger analysis.
rows.anchor: و { يوم هم بارزون } بدل من { يوم التلاقي } . و { هم بارزون } جملة اسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person pronoun refers back to the disbelievers mentioned in 40:14.
rows.anchor: وضمير الغيبة عائد إلى { الكافرون من قوله : ولو كره الكافرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that nothing is hidden from Allah explains their appearing: their outward and inward states are wholly manifest.
rows.anchor: وجملة { لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء } بيان لجملة { هم بارزون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit name Allah is clearer because its antecedent is remote in the ensuing phrase about whom He wills among His servants; the subject of warn most likely refers to that relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وإظهار اسم الجلالة لأن إظهاره أصرح لبعد معاده بما عقبه من قوله : { على من يشاء من عباده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minhum means the whole group and their circumstances; the plural pronoun permits an understood modifier suited to context.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { منهم } من مجموعهم ، أي من مجموع أحوالهم وشؤونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word shayʾ is maximally general, so nothing in their outward or inward states is hidden; the wording is broader than saying no person is hidden.
rows.anchor: وأوثر أيضا لفظ { شيء } لتوغله في العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question and answer are introduced through an omitted verb of saying: Allah is understood to say, Who owns sovereignty today, either as a circumstantial clause or a rhetorical restart.
rows.anchor: مقول لقول محذوف ، وحذف القول من حديث البحر . والتقدير : يقول الله لمن الملك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may make tyrants acknowledge that their earthly claims of power for idols or themselves were false, exemplified by pagan deities, Pharaoh, and royal titles.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام إما تقريري ليشهد الطغاة من أهل المحشر على أنفسهم أنهم كانوا في الدنيا مخطئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question also rebukes idolaters who assigned different gods to particular peoples and domains, including the Greeks, Egyptians, and Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: مثل قول اليونان بإلاه البحر وإلاه الحرب وإلاه الحكمة ، وقول أقباط مصر بإلاه الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report about the Resurrection has God say, I am the King; where are the kings of earth? Ibn ʿĀshūr reads this as frightening earthly rulers by asking where their grandeur has gone.
rows.anchor: ثم يقول الله أنا الملك أين ملوك الأرض ) استفهاما مرادا منه تخويفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may build anticipation for its answer, so the answer settles more deeply in the listener; the question to the Prophet’s servants in 2:186 is a parallel.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون الاستفهام كناية عن التشويق إلى ما يرد بعده من الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yawm means the present day relative to the time when the reported statement is uttered.
rows.anchor: و { اليوم } المعرف باللام هو اليوم الحاضر ، وحضوره بالنسبة إلى القول المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone may be the rest of the same divine utterance, with the speaker answering His own rhetorical question.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من بقية القول المقدر الصادر من جانب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a separate omitted speech has the people present answer that sovereignty belongs to Allah the One, the Subduer.
rows.anchor: أي فيقول المسؤولون : { لله الواحد القهار } إقرارا منهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names One and Subduer suit the question of sovereignty because the scene displays Allah’s unity and His domination of tyrants and despots.
rows.anchor: وذكر الصفتين { الواحد القهار } دون غيرهما من الصفات العلى لأن لمعنييهما مزيد مناسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three following clauses remain connected to the divine utterance, whether the previous answer is one speech or an answer by the gathered people.
rows.anchor: لا ريب في أن هذه الجمل الثلاث متصلة بالمقول الصادر من جانب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses progress from divine ownership to its effects: every soul is judged for its deeds, without injustice, and with swift reckoning; God is not distracted from justice and needs no deliberation. The judgment clause explains ownership, and the no-injustice clause specifies its fairness.
rows.anchor: جملة { اليوم تجزى } الخ واقعة موقع البيان لما في جملة { لمن الملك اليوم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arinā means show us; it covertly expresses their desire to take revenge on the two misleaders, and the response is conditional: if shown them, they will put them underfoot.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { أرنا } عين لنا ، وهو كناية عن إرادة انتقامهم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting them underfoot means trampling and kicking each misleader by members of the followers’ larger mass; the masses outnumber leaders, and kicking with feet was vengeance and humiliation.
rows.anchor: والجعل تحت الأقدام : الوطء بالأقدام والرفس ، أي نجعل آحادهم تحت أقدام آحاد جماعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Waʿla al-Jurmi’s verse illustrates trampling in anger, supporting the description of foot-kicking as humiliation and revenge.
rows.anchor: وكان الوطء بالأرجل من كيفيات الانتقام والامتهان ، قال ابن وعلة الجرمي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to see the misleaders because those leaders occupy lower levels of Hell than their followers and are therefore out of sight.
rows.anchor: وإنما طلبوا أن يروهما لأن المضلين كانوا في دركات من النار أسفل من دركات أتباعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that they become the lowest prepares for God to show them the leaders: the followers know God is angrier at the misleaders, and call them lower to mean more contemptible and humiliated.
rows.anchor: والتعليل { ليكونا من الأسفلين } توطئة لاستجابة الله تعالى لهم أن يريهموهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce arinā with kasra on rāʾ; Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Sūsī from Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb use sukūn to lighten the kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { أرنا } بكسر الراء . وقرأه ابن كثير وابن عامر والسوسي عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl distinguishes the readings: kasra means show it to me, while sukūn means give it to me; the latter makes their request to be enabled to humiliate the misleaders.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : بصرنيه ، وإذا قلته بسكون الراء فهو استعطاء ، معناه : أعطنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr doubles the nūn in alladhayni, a dialectal form also found in the discussion of 4:16.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير { اللذين } بتشديد النون من اسم الموصول وهي لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing past nations’ worldly punishment and the afterlife threat to Meccan deniers, the audience expects to hear the believers’ fate; 41:30 answers with good news.
rows.anchor: تشوف السامع إلى معرفة حظ المؤمنين ووصفف حالهم فجاء قوله : { إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening particle inn responds to polytheists’ denial, and its emphasis further rebukes them.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح الجملة بحرف التوكيد منظور فيه إلى إنكار المشركين ذلك ، ففي توكيد الخبر زيادة قمع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying our Lord is Allah means publicly declaring tawḥīd without fearing anyone; it expresses actual conviction, since speech is presumed truthful and matched to reality.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { قالوا ربنا الله } أنهم صدعوا بذلك ولم يخشوا أحدا بإعلانهم التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Our Lord is Allah implies exclusivity: no lord but Allah. Tawḥīd removes the obstacle that kept polytheists from accepting the Messenger’s teaching, namely the command to abandon worship of other gods.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ربنا الله } يفيد الحصر بتعريف المسند إليه والمسند ، أي لا رب لنا إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists’ denial of resurrection was inherited from the advocates of associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: ولأن التكذيب بالبعث تلقوه من دعاة الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiqāma literally means having no crookedness or deviation; the added sīn and tāʾ intensify the sense of being upright.
rows.anchor: والاستقامة حقيقتها : عدم الاعوجاج والميلل ، والسين والتاء فيها للمبالغة في التقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By metaphor, istiqāma covers good conduct and a life on truth and honesty; the phrase can also mean that a land obeyed its king. Here it includes fulfilling obligations, first by remaining firm in tawḥīd without changing or recanting.
rows.anchor: وتطلق الاستقامة بوجه الاستعارة على ما يجمع معنى حسن العمل والسيرة على الحق والصدق

rows.speaker: سفيان الثقفي
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thaqafi asked the Prophet for a concise statement about Islam that would make further questioning unnecessary; the Prophet said to believe in Allah and then remain upright.
rows.anchor: قل آمنت بالله ثم استقم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr explained then remained upright as not associating anything with Allah.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر { ثم استقاموا } : لم يشركوا بالله شيئا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar explained it as staying on the path in obedience to God and not turning aside like foxes.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر : استقاموا على الطريقة لطاعته ثم لم يروغوا روغان الثعالب

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman explained it as making one’s deeds sincere for Allah.
rows.anchor: وقال عثمان : ثم أخلصوا العمل لله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali explained it as performing the obligatory duties.
rows.anchor: وعن علي : ثم أدوا الفرائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four caliphs’ explanations all return to uprightness in faith and its effects; their attention to the verse highlights how important istiqāma is in religion.
rows.anchor: فقد تولى تفسير هذه الآية الخلفاء الأربعة رضي الله عنهم . وكل هذه الأقوال ترجع إلى معنى الاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a relative clause rather than simply saying believers hints that their claim and uprightness cause the angels’ descent and honor; true belief and righteous action bring success.
rows.anchor: لما في الصلة من الإيماء إلى أنها سبب ثبوت المسند للمسند إليه فيفيد أن تنزل الملائكة عليهم بتلك الكرامة مسبب على قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks a rank-order delay: istiqāma exceeds the confession of tawḥīd because it includes preserving tawḥīd and acting on what it requires, confirming the confession came from real knowledge.
rows.anchor: و { ثم } للتراخي الرتبي لأن الاستقامة زائدة في المرتبة على الإقرار بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses express the two foundations of Islamic perfection: knowing the truth to receive guidance and knowing the good in order to act, yielding certain knowledge and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: وجمع قوله : { قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا } أصلي الكمال الإسلامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Our Lord is Allah signifies knowledge of God’s divinity as the foundation of certain knowledge; istiqāma signifies the foundation of good action: holding to truth in the middle, away from excess and neglect.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { قالوا ربنا الله } مشير إلى الكمال النفساني وهو معرفة الحق للاهتداء به ، ومعرفة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path avoids theological extremes: denial of attributes until negation, affirming them until anthropomorphism, fatalism or libertarianism, despair or presumption; in conduct it avoids excess and neglect.
rows.anchor: على أن كمال الإعتقاد راجع إلى الاستقامة ، فالاعتقاد الحق أن لا يتوغل في جانب النفي إلى حيث ينتهي إلى التعطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels may descend at the Resurrection, as the believers’ promised Paradise and direct address suggest; this contrasts with the angels driving God’s enemies in 41:19.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون في وقت الحشر كما دل عليه قولهم : { التي كنتم توعدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection two guardian angels who recorded each believer’s earthly deeds descend for them, honoring believers like prophets and messengers; enemies find angels present to drive them, not descending for their sake.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أنه يتنزل على كل مؤمن ملكان هما الحافظان اللذان كانا يكتبان أعماله في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because tanazzul includes speech, the following an is explanatory: the angels are understood to say, Do not fear or grieve.
rows.anchor: ولتضمن { تتنزل } معنى القول وردت بعده ( أن ) التفسيرية والتقدير : يقولون لا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, angels descend invisibly in worldly life, their effect felt in believers’ hearts: they instill serenity, recall Paradise, counter satanic whispering, and prompt rejection of allegiance outside God’s party, paralleling 41:25.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تنزل الملائكة عليهم في الدنيا ، وهو تنزل خفي يعرف بحصول آثاره في نفوس المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the worldly-descent reading, perfected believers fear only God, do not grieve over affliction, trust that all is decreed, and rejoice in the coming grace of God.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن المؤمنين الكاملين لا يخافون غير الله ، ولا يحزنون على ما يصيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the worldly reading, kāna in the promised Paradise phrase intensifies the promise, while the present/future tense remains current; the angels’ declaration of friendship supports them now and promises help later.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى فقوله : { التي كنتم } تعتبر ( كان ) فيه مزيدة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not fear is a prohibition of fear’s cause, expecting harm; it assures believers that Allah will not punish them, removing fear through divine security conveyed by the angels.
rows.anchor: و { لا } ناهية ، والمقصود من النهي عن الخوف : النهي عن سببه ، وهو توقع الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is distress caused by expecting a severe harm; grief is distress caused by losing a benefit or experiencing harm.
rows.anchor: والخوف : غم في النفس ينشأ عن ظن حصول مكروه شديد . والحزن : غم في النفس ينشأ عن وقوع مكروه بفواتت نفعع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels add glad tidings after reassurance because joy in bliss is complete when it is not mixed with expectation of harm.
rows.anchor: وألحقوا بتأمينهم بشارتهم ، لأن وقع النعيم في النفس موقع المسرة إذا لم يخالطه توقع المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Paradise the one they were promised recalls the deeds that earned it and gives them immediate joy in God’s approval and fulfillment of His promise; kāna presents them as rooted in that promise through prior faith and deeds.
rows.anchor: ووصف الجنة ب { التي كنتم توعدون } تذكير لهم بأعمالهم التي وعدوا عليها بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense in you are promised implies repeated promises, through repeated promised deeds and recurring reminders and glad tidings.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بالمضارع في { توعدون } إفادة أنهم قد تكرر وعدهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We are your allies introduces the angels to comfort believers; recognizing an old companion eases the arrival’s surprise, loneliness, and unease before a host.
rows.anchor: وقول الملائكة : { نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة } تعريف بأنفسهم للمؤمنين تأنيسا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are the angels who accompanied believers in worldly life, recorded their good deeds, and testified to their prayer; the report says angels alternate night and day and tell God they left His servants praying.
rows.anchor: إذ كانوا يكتبون حسناتهم ويشهدون عند الله بصلاتهم كما في حديث : ( يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels kept their covenant and became allies in the hereafter; their assurance interrupts the Paradise descriptions so believers know their good news comes from loving companions glad for their welfare.
rows.anchor: وقد حفظوا العهد فكانوا أولياء المؤمنين في الآخرة ، وقد جيء بهذا القول معترضا بين صفات الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly angel-companions parallel the companions assigned to disbelievers in 41:25: the latter’s followers voice blame, while angels voice praise for believers.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قوله : { في الحياة الدنيا } إشارة إلى مقابلة قوله في المشركين { وقيضنا لهم قرناء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Nāji says guardian angels are specific to believers, making their friendship clear.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الحفظة من خصائص المؤمنين كما نقله ابن ناجي في ( شرح الرسالة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority hold that guardian angels serve believers and unbelievers, a reading supported by al-Infitar 82:9–12; this makes the ally angels in 41:31 a separate class protecting believers in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الحفظة موكلين على المؤمنين والكافرين كما مشى عليه الجمهور وهو ظاهر قوله تعالى : { كلا بل تكذبون بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The class of angels protecting believers in worldly life may be the muʿaqqibāt mentioned in al-Raʿd 13:11.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون هذا الصنف من الملائكة هو المسمى بالمعقبات في قوله تعالى : { له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه

none: Qur’anic text only; no exegetical claim to record.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah will exact revenge on the deniers in this life whether the Prophet is alive or has died; vengeance belongs to God because they rejected His command and religion, also answering the Prophet’s concern and the deniers’ wish for his death.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أننا منتقمون منهم في الدنيا سواء كنت حيا أو بعد موتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After easing the Prophet’s distress over their unbelief and promising victory, God commands him to remain firm in his religion and Scripture rather than lose resolve at their stubborn rejection.
rows.anchor: فرع على ذلك أن أمره بالثبات على دينه وكتابه وأن لا يخور عزمه في الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istimsāk means holding tightly; its added letters intensify the meaning.
rows.anchor: والاستمساك : شدة المسك ، فالسين والتاء فيه للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet is already holding revelation, the command asks him to persist; Arabic blessings that someone remain honored illustrate this durative use, as does the prayer to be guided to the straight path in 1:6.
rows.anchor: والأمر به مستعمل في طلب الدوام ، لأن الأمر بفعل لمن هو متلبس به لا يكون لطلب الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation he must hold fast to is the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والذي أوحي إليه هو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is acting on revelation; saying the Prophet is on it, rather than simply calling the path straight, portrays him as firmly guided without hesitation or fear of straying.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم : هو العمل بالذي أوحي إليه ، فكأنه قيل : إنه صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet is on a straight path confirms and explains the command to hold fast to revelation.
rows.anchor: وجملة { إنك على صراط مستقيم } تأييد لطلب الاستمساك بالذي أوحي إليه وتعليل له
